text:
maria: Heads-up — after the continuous-batching switch last night I'm seeing a strange interaction with prefix caching. Hit-rate on production for common prefixes fell from ~82% -> ~63% for prefixes >32 tokens, and p95 latency for small single-turn requests increased ~18ms.

dave: 😬 do you have a repro or perf run?

maria: Quick summary: the new batcher started mixing long-context (L=2048) and short-context (L<=128) requests in the same continuous batch. That changed batch composition so KV caches got populated with long-lived KV entries that then got evicted when the short requests came through, which appears to break the primary prefix keying heuristic we rely on.

infra-bot: deploy #prod-batcher v2.7 rolled out at 1807600000 — telemetry: continuous-batching enabled, dynamic-mix=on.

sophie: Hmm. Kernel selection might also be involved — when batch contains mixed seq lengths we fall back to conservative matmul kernels causing higher per-token latency. Are you seeing kernel fallback traces?

maria: Yes — perf traces show alternation between fast-f32-int8 kernels and a slower generic kernel whenever the batch composition changed mid-iter. That alternation also seems to cause KV cache thrash because KV footprints differ across kernels (different kv layout/stripe sizes).

aj: Can you paste the sampling flame? Even a tiny snippet helps.

maria: Pasted a short snippet from the profiler below (stackwalk simplified):
```
batcher::compose_batch() -> continuous::enqueue() -> runtime::select_kernel(batch) [switch f32_fast <-> generic] -> decoder::kv_access(prefix_key) -> cache_miss -> load_from_storage()
```

maria: Also attaching the hit-rate numbers from the last 6h: common_prefixes(top-100) hit-rate 82% -> 63%, overall token-level hit-rate 71% -> 58%.

dry: suggestion: canonicalize prefix keying to be length-agnostic? e.g., hash(prompt_text + normalized_trailing_ws) so mixing kernels doesn't change keys.

sophie: Canonicalization helps but won't fix eviction pressure. If long sequences allocate larger KV-chunks, the cache size/per-entry accounting needs to be stable across kernel variants. We should normalize the KV entry accounting to 'logical tokens' rather than bytes.

aj: Another lever: change batching heuristic to be prefix-affinity first. Keep a small time window (5ms) where the batcher groups identical-prefix requests. That sacrifices a bit of batch fullness but keeps hit-rate high. We tested a variant in canary and saw hit-rate recover ~+14pp and p95 drop 12ms for small requests.

ryan: We implemented a lightweight 'prefix-affinity score' in the batcher: score = freq_in_window * prefix_length_penalty. If score>threshold we pin next N micro-batches to the prefix. Works well on traffic with heavy tail of repeated prompts.

maria: For regressions root-causing — I think two things aligned: 1) dynamic-mix on continuous batcher made mixed-length batches common, 2) KV cache accounting was byte-based and not normalized, 3) kernel selection switching caused different KV layouts.

sophie: Proposed repo actions:
- normalize KV accounting to logical-token units (PR ready)
- add prefix-affinity bucket to continuous batcher (experiment branch)
- add kernel-stability penalty in select_kernel (prefer same kernel if batch composition has prefix affinity)
- add synthetic warmup in Dedicated to pre-populate common prefixes on cold starts

maria: Quick config we used in the canary:
```json
{
  "continuous_batcher": {
    "affinity_window_ms": 5,
    "affinity_threshold": 12,
    "max_pinned_batches": 3
  },
  "kv_cache": {
    "accounting_mode": "logical_tokens"
  },
  "kernel_selection": {
    "stability_bias": 0.7
  }
}
```

dave: Nice. Did the canary show any throughput regressions?

maria: Throughput was ~-4% during micro-bursts (because we sometimes wait the 5ms window), but overall token/sec unchanged and cost per token improved due to fewer loads and lower p95 tail.

aj: A small perf note: warmup by replaying the top-200 prefixes for each model on deploy reduced cold-start misses by ~70% in nightly canary. We used rate-limited synthetic requests to avoid polluting metrics.

ryan: Action items:
- PR for kv accounting normalizer (sophie)
- experiment branch for affinity batching + kernel stability bias (aj + infra)
- add synthetic warmup job to deploy pipeline (maria)
- add dashboard metric: prefix_affinity_score and KV_eviction_rate (dave)

maria: I'll open the bug/regression issue with links to traces and hit-rate dumps. If we get the affinity + normalized accounting in, we should be able to revert dynamic-mix or keep it with conservative defaults.

dave: Thanks — please tag me in the issue.

infra-bot: NOTE: rolling back batcher v2.7 is an option but will affect throughput for long-context workloads. Recommended: try affinity patch first on canary. :thumbsup:

maria: filing issue now: https://redwood.internal/issue/INF-2048 (contains perf traces and sample payloads).

aj: ok I can pick up the batcher experiment tomorrow.

sophie: I'll land the accounting PR after a quick unit test for token->byte mapping.

maria: Great — thanks everyone.
